_comment: UK road marking rules. Every number is tuned by eye later; each rule carries a `source` note. Source keys: 'DfT TSM Ch5' = docs/road-marking-rules.md (Traffic Signs Manual chapter 5 sections 1-5); 'estimate' = not in that reference, a sensible placeholder. Speeds are in speed_unit (mph). Conditions (`if`): speed_max (<=), speed_min (>), width_min/width_max (driving-lane carriageway width, m), lanes_min/lanes_max (driving lanes, both directions), shoulder, one_way. A selector is a plain value or a list of {if, style|value}; the first match wins; style "" means no marking. Lane-type strings may list alternatives with '|'; boundary rules match either order of the two lanes; 'outside' is the area beyond the cross-section.
_min_mark_source: estimate: nothing shorter than 0.3 m is ever painted

centre_low.source: DfT TSM Ch5: centre line 2 m mark / 4 m gap at 40 mph or less, 100 mm

centre_high.source: DfT TSM Ch5: centre line 3 m / 6 m above 40 mph

centre_wide_low.source: DfT TSM Ch5: 150 mm on roads 10 m or more wide

centre_wide_high.source: DfT TSM Ch5: 150 mm on roads 10 m or more wide

warning_low.source: DfT TSM Ch5: warning line (inverse of centre line) 4 m / 2 m at 40 mph or less

warning_high.source: DfT TSM Ch5: warning line 6 m / 3 m above 40 mph

warning_wide_low.source: DfT TSM Ch5: 150 mm on roads 10 m or wider and on four or six lanes

warning_wide_high.source: DfT TSM Ch5: 150 mm on roads 10 m or wider and on four or six lanes

lane_low.source: DfT TSM Ch5: lane line 6 m module at 40 mph or less; mark/gap split is an estimate (the reference says confirm against TSRGD)

lane_high.source: DfT TSM Ch5: lane line 9 m module above 40 mph; mark/gap split is an estimate

lane_high_150.source: DfT TSM Ch5: always 150 mm on 70 mph dual carriageways and motorways

edge_100.source: DfT TSM Ch5: edge line 100 mm continuous, no hard shoulder

edge_150.source: DfT TSM Ch5: edge line 150 mm (70 mph without a shoulder, or with a hard strip)

edge_200.source: DfT TSM Ch5: edge line 200 mm on motorways and 70 mph roads with a shoulder or strip

double_white.source: DfT TSM Ch5 diagram 1013.1: two continuous lines 175 mm apart, 100 mm each

bay_line.source: estimate: parking bay line (Chapter 3 not extracted), 100 mm continuous

give_way_low.source: estimate: give way line (diagram 1003), 200 mm broken, 600/300 (Chapter 3 not extracted)

give_way_high.source: estimate: give way line on faster roads, 300 mm broken, 1000/500

zebra_give_way.source: estimate: zebra approach give way line

fill_white.source: filled polygons (triangle, stripes, arrows) use the colour only

zones.source: DfT TSM Ch5: warning line replaces the centre line on junction approaches; minimum marks 5 at 30 mph, 7 above (10 on four or six lanes)

boundaries.source: DfT TSM Ch5: no centre line under about 5.5 m. Choice (estimate): urban streets (the reference does not cover parked residential streets) have no centre line along their length below 7.3 m wide, only the warning line on junction approaches; wider urban streets keep a centre line

zones.source: DfT TSM Ch5: lane lines become warning lines on approaches to give way lines, signals and roundabouts

boundaries.source: DfT TSM Ch5: lane line between same-direction lanes
estimate: continuous line along the parking lane

bays.source: length: estimate (6 m bays); keepout: Highway Code rule 243 (no parking within 10 m of a junction)

zones.source: DfT TSM Ch5: warning line on junction approaches
DfT TSM Ch5: warning line (or double white where visibility is limited, carriageway at least 6.1 m, not built-up) on bends; radius threshold 200 m is an estimate

boundaries.source: DfT TSM Ch5: centre line only on carriageways of at least 5.5 m

zones.source: DfT TSM Ch5: lane lines become warning lines on approaches

boundaries.source: DfT TSM Ch5: edge line 100 mm (150 mm at 70 mph) 225 mm in from the carriageway edge; no edge line against a kerb

zones.source: DfT TSM Ch5 dual carriageway junction: lane lines through the junction are warning lines, at least 7 marks at 40 mph or above and 5 below

boundaries.source: DfT TSM Ch5: lane lines 150 mm on 70 mph dual carriageways
DfT TSM Ch5: with a hard shoulder or strip 150 mm (200 mm at 70 mph), 225 mm in from the carriageway edge

zones.source: DfT TSM Ch5: lane lines become warning lines on approaches, at least 7 marks

boundaries.source: DfT TSM Ch5: always 150 mm on motorways
DfT TSM Ch5: motorway edge line 200 mm, 225 mm in from the carriageway edge

give_way.source: estimate: dimensions from memory of diagrams 1003 / 1023 (Chapter 3 not extracted); setback keeps the line outside the junction trim

stop_line.source: estimate: only made for arms the caller names (no signal or sight-line data in v0)

zebra.source: estimate: 500 mm stripes, 600 mm gaps (500-700 mm in the regulations), band 3 m (2.4 m minimum); no studs or zig-zags (Chapter 6 not extracted)

roundabout_entry.source: estimate: give way line across the entering lanes (roundabout markings not extracted from the Manual)

gore.source: Pattern choice follows the owner (traditional practice): chevrons (TSRGD diagram 1042, as remembered; docs/road-marking-rules.md does not extract it) where traffic passes the nose in the same direction on both sides (merge, diverge); diagonal hatching (diagrams 1040 family) where opposing flows are separated. Both are bordered by a continuous line. Estimates: chevron wing angle 35 degrees, 0.3 m stripes at 1.2 m pitch, apex pointing the way the traffic travels; edge lines continue through the slip at the edge-line width

arrows.source: DfT TSM Ch5: single-headed lane arrows 4 m (4/2 module), 6 m (6/3), 9 m at 70 mph, at least two per lane; distances from the junction are an estimate
